definitions.explanation: The general direction or course that a plan, project, organization, or piece of work is taking or should take.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{方向性|ほうこうせい}を{決|き}める。
チームの{方向性|ほうこうせい}が{合|あ}わない。
{議論|ぎろん}を{重|かさ}ねて、ようやくプロジェクトの{方向性|ほうこうせい}が{見|み}えてきた。
examples.english: After repeated discussions, the direction of the project has finally come into view.

notes:
Compound of {方向|ほうこう} (direction) + the suffix {性|せい} (-ness, nature of). Usually abstract — the course of a plan or group rather than a physical direction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {方向性|ほうこうせい}を{決|き}める: to decide on a direction
- {方向性|ほうこうせい}を{示|しめ}す: to set out a course
- {方向性|ほうこうせい}が{合|あ}う: to have aligned aims

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {方針|ほうしん}: policy; course of action — a concrete decided plan, more definite than {方向性|ほうこうせい}
- {方向|ほうこう}: direction — can be literal (physical) as well as abstract
